quests.hint: Say hello and give your own name.
quests.explanation: Trading names straight after a greeting keeps the exchange balanced, so you are not only receiving information.
quests.partnerDialogue: Hi there! I'm Tom, I live next door.
quests.sampleAnswer: Nice to meet you. I'm Aisha.
acceptedSynonyms: nice to meet you. i'm aisha
hello, tom. my name is aisha
nice to meet you. i am aisha
smartReplies: Nice to meet you. I'm Aisha.
Hello, Tom. My name is Aisha.
quests.correctAnswer: Nice to meet you. I'm Aisha.

quests.hint: Tell the receptionist your first name and surname.
quests.explanation: When someone has just asked for your name, "It's..." sounds more natural than repeating "My name is".
quests.partnerDialogue: Welcome to Fit Gym. Can I have your name, please?

quests.hint: Say you are happy to meet them too.
quests.explanation: The little word "too" sends the same feeling back, so you don't just repeat their sentence.
quests.partnerDialogue: Nice to meet you.

quests.instruction: Answer, then ask one question back.
quests.hint: Say you're fine and ask how they are.
quests.explanation: Returning the question ("And you?") keeps small talk moving. A bare answer can feel like the end of the conversation.
quests.partnerDialogue: Hey, how's it going?

quests.hint: Say you're okay and give a short reason.
quests.explanation: A short reason after "I'm okay" shows you understand the concern and calms the other person.
quests.partnerDialogue: You look tired. Are you okay?
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm fine, just tired. I went to bed late.
acceptedSynonyms: i'm fine, just tired. i went to bed late
yes, a little. i didn't sleep well
yes, i'm okay. i went to bed late
i am fine, just tired. i went to bed late
smartReplies: Yes, a little. I didn't sleep well.
Yes, I'm okay. I went to bed late.
I'm fine, just tired. I went to bed late.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm fine, just tired. I went to bed late.

quests.hint: Say the weekend was nice and mention one thing you did.
quests.explanation: Answering a yes/no question plus one detail gives your partner something to react to.
quests.partnerDialogue: Did you have a good weekend?
quests.sampleAnswer: It was great, thanks. I saw a film.
acceptedSynonyms: it was great, thanks. i saw a film
yes, it was nice. i visited my aunt
yes, thanks. i stayed home and rested
smartReplies: It was great, thanks. I saw a film.
Yes, it was nice. I visited my aunt.
Yes, thanks. I stayed home and rested.
quests.correctAnswer: It was great, thanks. I saw a film.

quests.hint: Ask for some water.
quests.explanation: "Could I have..." plus "please" is softer than just naming the thing you want.
quests.partnerDialogue: Are you ready to order?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could I have some water first, please?
acceptedSynonyms: could i have some water first, please
can i have water first, please
just some water for now, please
smartReplies: Can I have water first, please?
Could I have some water first, please?
quests.correctAnswer: Could I have some water first, please?

quests.instruction: Say what you are looking for.
quests.hint: Ask where the restroom is.
quests.explanation: English has several words for this room (restroom, toilet, bathroom). All are fine, and "Excuse me" is a good way to begin.
quests.partnerDialogue: Hi! Can I help you with something?
quests.sampleAnswer: Yes. Excuse me, where is the toilet?
acceptedSynonyms: yes. excuse me, where is the toilet
smartReplies: Yes. Excuse me, where is the toilet?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes. Excuse me, where is the toilet?

quests.hint: You forgot your pen. Ask to borrow one.
quests.explanation: "Can I borrow...?" is for something you will give back, so it fits a pen, not a snack.
quests.partnerDialogue: You look worried. What's the matter?
quests.sampleAnswer: My pen is gone. Could I borrow one?
acceptedSynonyms: my pen is gone. could i borrow one
i don't have a pen. can i use yours
i lost my pen. can i borrow yours
smartReplies: I don't have a pen. Can I use yours?
My pen is gone. Could I borrow one?
I lost my pen. Can I borrow yours?
quests.correctAnswer: My pen is gone. Could I borrow one?

quests.hint: Tell them the seat is free.
quests.explanation: A clear "No" here means "not taken". Adding "go ahead" avoids confusion.
quests.partnerDialogue: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
acceptedSynonyms: no, it is free. please sit

quests.instruction: Answer and add a little more.
quests.hint: Say the umbrella is yours and thank them.
quests.explanation: Adding thanks turns a yes/no answer into a friendly reply.
quests.partnerDialogue: Excuse me, is this your umbrella?
acceptedSynonyms: yes, it's mine. thanks so much
oh yes, that's mine. thank you
yes, it is mine. thank you
smartReplies: Yes, it's mine. Thanks so much!
Oh yes, that's mine. Thank you!

quests.instruction: Be honest and ask for help.
quests.hint: Be honest about your level and ask for help understanding.
quests.explanation: "A little" is an honest answer. Asking for slower speech is a survival skill worth using every day.
quests.partnerDialogue: Do you speak English?
quests.sampleAnswer: Yes, but only a little. Slowly, please.
acceptedSynonyms: yes, but only a little. slowly, please
smartReplies: Yes, but only a little. Slowly, please.
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, but only a little. Slowly, please.

quests.instruction: Answer with your country and one more detail.
quests.hint: Say which country you come from and the city.
quests.explanation: Adding a city gives the other person something more specific to ask about next.
quests.partnerDialogue: So, where are you from?
acceptedSynonyms: i come from brazil. from recife
smartReplies: I come from Brazil. From Recife.

quests.hint: Spell the surname Khan.
quests.explanation: Say each letter separately and slowly. Stress the letters that sound alike.
quests.partnerDialogue: How do you spell your last name?

quests.hint: Say you are a nurse and where you work.
quests.explanation: A job answer with "I'm a..." plus the workplace gives a complete picture in two short sentences.
quests.partnerDialogue: So, what do you do?
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm a nurse at a hospital.
acceptedSynonyms: i'm a nurse at a hospital
i work as a nurse in a hospital
i'm a nurse. i work at a hospital
i am a nurse at a hospital
smartReplies: I'm a nurse at a hospital.
I work as a nurse in a hospital.
I'm a nurse. I work at a hospital.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm a nurse at a hospital.

quests.hint: The cashier hands you your change. Thank them.
quests.explanation: Adding "very much" or "a lot" makes thanks warmer than a quick "thanks".
quests.partnerDialogue: Here's your change, sir.
acceptedSynonyms: thank you. have a nice day
smartReplies: Thank you. Have a nice day.

quests.hint: Someone bumped into you. Tell them it's fine.
quests.explanation: English speakers use "No problem" or "It's okay" to show the mistake is small.
quests.partnerDialogue: Oh, sorry! I didn't see you.

quests.hint: A stranger thanks you for helping. Reply.
quests.explanation: "You're welcome" is right, but "Happy to help" sounds warmer and more natural in daily life.
quests.partnerDialogue: Thanks so much for helping me with these bags!

quests.hint: Choose tea. Be polite.
quests.explanation: Name your choice first when you're given two options. It's the information the other person needs most.
quests.partnerDialogue: Would you like tea or coffee?

quests.hint: Choose outside and say why.
quests.explanation: A short reason after your choice sounds natural and helps the waiter understand you.
quests.partnerDialogue: Would you like to sit inside or outside?
quests.sampleAnswer: I'd like to sit outside. The weather is nice.
acceptedSynonyms: i'd like to sit outside. the weather is nice
outside is better. it's a nice day
i would like to sit outside. the weather is nice
smartReplies: I'd like to sit outside. The weather is nice.
Outside is better. It's a nice day.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to sit outside. The weather is nice.

quests.hint: Pick the colour you prefer.
quests.explanation: For a choice between two things, "the blue one" avoids repeating the noun.
quests.partnerDialogue: Which do you like better, the red bag or the blue one?

quests.hint: Read the time aloud in a natural spoken way.
quests.explanation: "Half past three" and "three thirty" mean the same. Both are natural in speaking.
quests.partnerDialogue: Excuse me, do you know the time?
acceptedSynonyms: yes, it is half past three

quests.hint: Say the class is on Tuesday at six.
quests.explanation: English puts day before time: "Tuesday at six". Use "on" for days and "at" for clock times.
quests.partnerDialogue: When is the English class?
acceptedSynonyms: the class is tuesday at six
smartReplies: The class is Tuesday at six.

quests.instruction: Say yes and ask about the plan.
quests.hint: Say you're free on Saturday and ask what the plan is.
quests.explanation: Saying you're free is only half the reply. Asking about the plan shows interest.
quests.partnerDialogue: Are you free this Saturday?
quests.sampleAnswer: Yes, I am. What are we doing?
acceptedSynonyms: yes, i am. what are we doing
yes, i'm free. what's the plan
saturday? yes, i'm free. what's up
smartReplies: Yes, I'm free. What's the plan?
Saturday? Yes, I'm free. What's up?
Yes, I am. What are we doing?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, I am. What are we doing?

quests.hint: You want to know the price of a jacket.
quests.explanation: "How much is...?" for one item and "How much are...?" for more than one.
quests.partnerDialogue: Hello, can I help you?
quests.sampleAnswer: Yes, how much is this jacket?
acceptedSynonyms: yes, how much is this jacket
yes, please. what's the price of this jacket
yes. how much is the jacket
smartReplies: Yes, how much is this jacket?
Yes, please. What's the price of this jacket?
Yes. How much is the jacket?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, how much is this jacket?

quests.hint: Refuse the offer and give a quick reason.
quests.explanation: After "No, thanks", a short reason keeps a refusal friendly.
quests.partnerDialogue: Would you like a bag with that?
quests.sampleAnswer: No, it's okay. I have one.
acceptedSynonyms: no, it's okay. i have one
no, thanks. i have my own
no, thank you. i brought a bag
no, it is okay. i have one
smartReplies: No, thanks. I have my own.
No, thank you. I brought a bag.
No, it's okay. I have one.
quests.correctAnswer: No, it's okay. I have one.

quests.hint: Say you'll pay by card.
quests.explanation: Paying is a short exchange: give the one word the cashier needs, then "please".
quests.partnerDialogue: Cash or card?

quests.hint: Greet your friend's friend by name.
quests.explanation: Using the person's name straight away helps you remember it and sounds friendly.
quests.partnerDialogue: Ali, this is my friend Lena.
acceptedSynonyms: hi, lena. nice to meet you
hello, lena. good to meet you
smartReplies: Hi, Lena. Nice to meet you.
Hello, Lena. Good to meet you.

quests.hint: Tell them the stop is next to the bank.
quests.explanation: "Next to" is one of the easiest ways to place something for a stranger.
quests.partnerDialogue: Excuse me, where's the bus stop?
quests.sampleAnswer: Go straight. It's next to the bank.
acceptedSynonyms: go straight. it's next to the bank
the bus stop is next to the bank
it's over there, next to the bank
go straight. it is next to the bank
smartReplies: Go straight. It's next to the bank.
The bus stop is next to the bank.
It's over there, next to the bank.
quests.correctAnswer: Go straight. It's next to the bank.

quests.instruction: Answer, but show you are not certain.
quests.hint: Answer, but show you're not completely sure.
quests.explanation: "I think" tells the listener you are not 100% sure, which is honest and polite.
quests.partnerDialogue: Excuse me, which floor is the pharmacy on?
quests.sampleAnswer: It's on the second floor, I think.
acceptedSynonyms: it's on the second floor, i think
i think it's on the second floor
it is on the second floor, i think
smartReplies: It's on the second floor, I think.
I think it's on the second floor.
quests.correctAnswer: It's on the second floor, I think.
